name: llm_call
concept: A real chat model is asked to multiply 27611 by 2033 without any tool, and its answer is compared with the exact product.
limitation: One recorded run of a real model; the answer varies between runs and one call does not measure an error rate.
title: A model call

name: llm_to_agent
concept: A LangGraph model/tool loop lets a real model call a calculator through a ToolNode and answer from the observation.
limitation: One recorded run of a real model; outputs vary between runs, and one arithmetic task does not show how often the model chooses the tool.
title: From model to agent

name: structured_output
concept: with_structured_output constrains a real model's reply to a Pydantic calculator decision and shows the raw JSON and the parsed fields.
limitation: One recorded run of a real model; provider-side schema enforcement guarantees the shape, not that the expression is correct.
title: Structured output

name: validation
concept: A real model proposes a JSON action for two requests, and a Pydantic output parser accepts the calculator call and blocks the other proposal.
limitation: One recorded run of a real model; the schema only checks the shape and action name, and semantic and authorization checks remain application code.
title: Reject an invalid decision

name: agent_loop
concept: A bounded LangGraph loop lets a real model call a calculator repeatedly, deciding each step from the observations so far.
limitation: One recorded run of a real model; the number of steps and the wording of the final answer vary between runs.
title: The smallest agent loop

name: stopping
concept: A real model told to keep checking an order that never ships is stopped by an application step limit in a bounded LangGraph loop, in three runs.
limitation: The order-status tool is a stub that always returns pending; three runs of one model do not show how other models or prompts behave.
title: The agent that never finishes

name: workflow_vs_agent
concept: A fixed LangChain composition and a LangGraph agent with a real model summarize three documents, with model calls, tokens and time measured by a callback.
limitation: One recorded run; the documents and tools are toy fixtures, translation uses a real model, and timings depend on the provider.
title: Workflow vs agent

name: tool_calling
concept: A real model bound to a LangChain calculator tool proposes a call, and the application looks the tool up in its registry and runs it.
limitation: One recorded run of a real model with a single tool; it shows one proposal, not how reliably the model calls tools.
title: One tool

name: multiple_tools
concept: A real model must choose between two search tools for six questions, once with clear names and descriptions and once with vague ones, and selection accuracy is counted.
limitation: The search tools are never executed; six questions and one run per variant are too few to estimate accuracy precisely.
title: Tool selection

name: tool_errors
concept: A LangGraph ToolNode error handler turns a failing weather tool into either a bare None or a structured error, and a real model answers from each observation.
limitation: The timeout is simulated; one recorded run per handler, and retry and fallback policy is covered in Chapter 24.
title: Tool failure

name: context_quantity
concept: A ChatPromptTemplate chain asks a real model about one refund among up to 999 other orders, three times per placement, and reports the verdicts and input tokens.
limitation: The orders are synthetic; three trials per context with one model show this run's behaviour, not a general position effect.
title: Context quantity

name: context_selection
concept: A RunnableLambda select-to-budget stage feeds the top two facts to a real model, five times with a good ranking and five times with a corrupted one that drops the refund window.
limitation: Relevance scores are hand-written fixtures, not a learned ranker; verdicts under the corrupted ranking vary between runs.
title: Context selection

name: embeddings
concept: Ranks three policy documents for four queries by word overlap and by OpenAIEmbeddings in an InMemoryVectorStore; only the embeddings match paraphrased queries.
limitation: Four queries and three documents; the cosine scores are model-specific and say nothing about retrieval quality at scale.
title: Word counts vs embeddings

name: rag
concept: A prompt | model chain answers the refund question three times for each of four evidence arrangements built from two equally scored policies; the answer depends on what evidence is passed and how it is labelled.
limitation: Three trials per condition with one model; which undated ordering wins can change between runs, and faithfulness is not scored.
title: The smallest RAG pipeline

name: reranking
concept: A word-overlap first stage ranks the stale history passage first; a model judge called with batch rescores the candidates and promotes the current policy, but cannot recover it when k=1 drops it.
limitation: A prompted chat model serves as the reranker rather than a trained cross-encoder, and its 0-10 scores vary between runs.
title: Reranking

name: working_memory
concept: A LangGraph model/tool cycle on MessagesState solves a multiply-then-add task; when the model node sees only the goal instead of the accumulated messages, it repeats the calculator call until the step limit stops it.
limitation: Dropping memory is simulated by slicing the messages passed to the model; the observed repetition is one model's behavior on one task.
title: Working memory

name: long_term_memory
concept: A naive, a vague and an explicit model-judged write policy store five messages in InMemoryStore as semantic or episodic; recalled semantic facts then shape a later answer.
limitation: The store is in process, recall is a type filter rather than search, and the vague judge's choices vary between runs.
title: Episodic and semantic memory

name: procedural_memory
concept: A procedure read from InMemoryStore is injected into the system prompt of a tool-calling model, which picks a first action for an assertion failure and a timeout under no, good, bad and stale procedures.
limitation: Two trials per case; the tools are never executed, so only the first action choice is measured.
title: Procedural memory

name: context_compression
concept: A full transcript and a last-six-lines window feed a tool-calling model; with the window the approval requirement is lost and the model emails instead of asking for approval.
limitation: A sliding window is the only compressor tested; model-written summaries are not, and the tools are not executed.
title: Compress working context

name: memory_consolidation
concept: Plain and guarded model prompts consolidate preference episodes into one fact; a LangGraph conditional edge enforces the minimum-evidence threshold in code before the guarded model runs.
limitation: Three small episode sets; conflict detection is left to the model and was observed only on these examples.
title: Memory consolidation

name: mcp_calculator
concept: A tools/list entry from a simulated JSON-RPC server becomes a StructuredTool bound to a real model, which calls it for arithmetic and declines a delete request; tool and protocol errors are shown separately.
limitation: The server is simulated in process: no MCP SDK, transport or initialization handshake; langchain-mcp-adapters plays the adapter role in practice.
title: MCP-shaped tool in LangChain

name: react
concept: A LangGraph model/tool cycle with ToolNode in which a real model looks up a price, observes it, then calls the calculator to add 15% VAT before answering.
limitation: The price lookup is a one-item dictionary, and the step order and final wording come from the model and can vary between runs.
title: ReAct loop with observations

name: planning
concept: A prompt | model | JsonOutputParser planner writes a JSON tool plan, a validator rejects unknown tools before execution, and an executor runs the steps with placeholders.
limitation: In the observed runs the model never named an unavailable tool for the US-dollar goal; it invented a conversion inside the calculator step, which tool-availability validation cannot catch.
title: Plan validation and execution

name: plan_execute
concept: Three controllers drive a two-route world where Route A is secretly blocked: a reactive tool-calling loop, a LangGraph plan-first cycle that retries its failed step, and a cycle that routes back to the model planner after a failure.
limitation: A two-route toy environment with a four-action limit; the replanning trigger is a single rule on the observation text.
title: Plan, execute, replan

name: reflection
concept: A LangGraph critique node calls a real model critic (careful or hasty) on a right and a wrong profit draft; a conditional edge applies the revision only if it matches the calculator result, compared with always applying it.
limitation: The drafts are fixed texts, and the exact verifier exists only because the task is arithmetic; the hasty critic's regressions vary in value from run to run.
title: Reflection with a verification gate

name: tree_reasoning
concept: The model first answers the 2 -> 13 puzzle directly; then LangGraph Send fans out one branch per first move, a real model judge or an exact judge prunes, and code verifies the completed paths.
limitation: A one-level toy tree; the model judge's pruning varies between runs (sometimes it keeps the right branch), so three runs show only a small sample.
title: Tree search with a model judge

name: routing
concept: A LangGraph conditional edge routes seven labeled requests with keyword rules and with a real model router given plain and sharper route descriptions, scoring accuracy and weighted misroute cost.
limitation: Destinations only record the route; nothing is answered, and seven tasks are too few to measure router accuracy.
title: Task routing with a model router

name: model_routing
concept: A nano and a mini model answer arithmetic tasks; LangChain RunnableBranch implements length and oracle routers, and with_fallbacks escalates to the stronger model when an exact check fails.
limitation: Each model answers each task once and the strategies reuse those answers; costs are illustrative units, and whether the nano model fails the hard tasks varies by run.
title: Model routing and a cheap-first cascade

name: parallelism
concept: Three independent real model calls run sequentially and then with LangChain RunnableParallel, timing both; a conversion run in parallel with the rate lookup it depends on lacks the rate, while a piped sequence gets it.
limitation: The rate service is a one-second sleep; timings depend on network latency, and the model's reply without a rate varies.
title: Parallel model calls

name: fanout_fanin
concept: LangGraph Send fans out three real model reviewers of a proposal, a reducer collects their findings, and a barrier fan-in keeps every finding and names a branch that failed through a forced timeout, in contrast to an over-summarizing fan-in.
limitation: The failure is forced with a 0.01 s timeout on one reviewer; the bad fan-in's exact-string agreement rule is a deliberately weak stand-in.
title: Fan-out/fan-in of model reviewers

name: agent_as_tool
concept: A parent model agent calls a child LangGraph agent wrapped as a LangChain tool; the child searches with its own model and step budget (a recursion_limit) and returns a structured complete or incomplete result.
limitation: The search tool returns fixed texts; in the chained case the child sometimes gives up after one search instead of exhausting its budget, and the parent may call it repeatedly until its own step budget stops it.
title: Agent as tool

name: supervisor_workers
concept: A real model writes the worker order; a LangGraph supervisor routes with Command(goto=...) to a researcher and real model analyst and writer, and a dependency-aware supervisor repairs a bad hand-written order.
limitation: The researcher returns fixed evidence, and the supervisor follows the given order rather than replanning.
title: Supervisor and workers

name: hierarchy
concept: A LangGraph root runs team-lead subgraphs whose real model leads summarize worker reports in 10 or 6 words; the root checks whether a source-confidence caveat survives, and structured leads carry caveats in their own field.
limitation: Worker reports are fixed; whether a 6-word summary drops the caveat varies by run (some runs keep it every time), and the caveat check is a keyword match.
title: Hierarchy with lossy summaries

name: voting
concept: Real model voters, each reading one source, run as parallel LangGraph branches; a majority policy with tie detection is compared against ground truth for independent and correlated sources.
limitation: Correlation comes from voters reading the same misleading source; the sources are fixed texts and votes can vary between runs.
title: Voting with model voters

name: debate_judge
concept: Two debater nodes present fixed arguments for a right and a wrong product; a real model judge without tools (three trials) and a calculator-grounded judge run in parallel, with the right answer in each position.
limitation: The debaters' arguments are written by hand, not generated; the model judge's picks vary between runs.
title: Debate and judge

name: blackboard
concept: Real model workers extract facts from sources and publish them in parallel to a reducer-backed LangGraph blackboard that keeps every claim with provenance, resolves conflicts by source authority, and recomputes the total after a correction.
limitation: In-memory state only; no versioned compare-and-swap, task claiming or durable storage (see chapters/20/36_blackboard.py); the source texts are fixed.
title: Blackboard with model workers

name: agent_to_agent
concept: A LangGraph task lifecycle authorizes the caller and has a real model produce a JSON artifact, which validates under the v1 instructions and fails validation once the schema line is dropped.
limitation: The remote agent is an in-process graph: no network, agent-card discovery, real authentication or messageId deduplication.
title: Agent-to-agent task lifecycle

name: evaluation
concept: A real model answers four arithmetic questions in a LangChain batch, and the same answers are scored by exact match and by numeric match.
limitation: Four cases are far too few to estimate accuracy; the scores and the wrong product vary between runs.
title: Task evaluation

name: trajectory_eval
concept: Two real models run as LangGraph tool agents; each trajectory is compared with a reference path and checked by invariants (required tool, irrelevant, unauthorized, step limit).
limitation: Tool results are fixed stubs, and which tools each model calls varies between runs; one run per model shows the checks, not a reliable comparison.
title: Trajectory evaluation

name: llm_judge
concept: A real model judge scores labelled answers three times each against a rubric, and a pairwise judge is run in both answer orders as a swap test.
limitation: Four labelled answers and three trials are a tiny calibration set; agreement and position effects vary between runs.
title: LLM-as-judge

name: tracing
concept: LangChain callbacks record run_id/parent_run_id and real timings and token counts for a real tool-using LangGraph agent, rebuilt into a span tree.
limitation: Local callbacks only, with graph plumbing runs filtered out; no tracing backend, sampling or redaction, and the tools are in-process stubs.
title: Tracing

name: cost_latency
concept: Three real model calls of different lengths are timed and their tokens counted, first sequentially and then in a RunnableParallel, comparing branch work with wall-clock time.
limitation: Timings are single measurements that vary with network and provider load; tokens are reported, not converted into prices.
title: Cost and latency

name: retry_fallback
concept: LangChain with_retry retries injected timeouts with exponential backoff around a real model call, stops at once on a real model-not-found error, and with_fallbacks switches to a smaller real model.
limitation: The timeouts are injected, not real outages; the client's own built-in retries are still enabled for real transient errors.
title: Retry, backoff, fallback

name: idempotency
concept: A real LangGraph payment agent is asked to retry after a lost response: without an idempotency key the customer is charged twice, with a key once.
limitation: The payment server, the lost response and the ledger are in-process simulations; production needs an atomic, durable idempotency record.
title: Idempotency

name: checkpoint_resume
concept: A LangGraph pipeline whose every step is a real model call crashes at verify and resumes from the InMemorySaver checkpoint, but restarts when the source version has changed.
limitation: The crash is injected and InMemorySaver does not survive a process restart; the stale-source check is application code, not a LangGraph feature.
title: Checkpoint and resume

name: human_approval
concept: A real agent proposes send_email; a LangGraph interrupt pauses for approval bound to an action hash, blocking rejection, a recipient changed after review, and an expired approval.
limitation: The reviewer's decisions and the elapsed time are scripted, and the email tool does not send anything.
title: Human approval

name: permissions
concept: A real agent, told nothing about permissions, picks a draft or send tool; a LangGraph conditional edge gates the call and the send tool re-checks permission itself.
limitation: Permissions are a static in-process table with no identity system or scoped credentials, and the tools do not send email.
title: Permissions

name: prompt_injection
concept: A real tool-calling ChatOpenAI model summarizes a page that contains an injected instruction; without a gate its send_email proposals run, with a task-scoped gate only the granted summarize tool executes.
limitation: The gate enforces authority from the task, it does not detect injection; whether the model obeys the page varies between runs, and the email tool only records recipients.
title: Prompt injection

name: memory_poisoning
concept: A real model writes preferences into a LangGraph InMemoryStore with their sources, and a later real agent picks a report recipient from recalled memory; a write policy that drops unauthenticated sources keeps the injected address out.
limitation: The 'authenticated' flag is a fixture, not verified identity, and the email is never sent; the store is in memory only.
title: Memory poisoning

name: sandboxing
concept: A real model writes three probe programs that a LangChain tool runs in a child process with an empty environment, a temp directory and a 1 s timeout; the secret and the runaway loop are contained, the host file read is not.
limitation: This is deliberately NOT a sandbox: the child runs as the host user with filesystem and network access; real isolation needs a container, microVM or OS sandbox.
title: Sandboxing

name: resource_budgets
concept: A real research agent in a LangGraph loop asks for searches that return only secondary sources; an admission node checks step and cost budgets before every search and stops with BUDGET_EXHAUSTED instead of overspending.
limitation: Search results and costs are fixtures in abstract units; how many searches the model attempts varies, so which budget trips varies between runs.
title: Resource budgets

name: autonomy_envelope
concept: A real model writes an action plan as structured output, and a LangGraph gate checks permissions, a cost budget and a cumulative risk budget that contracts when sensitive data appears, escalating actions that individual checks would allow.
limitation: No action is executed against a real system, risk scores are illustrative, and escalation only stops the graph rather than reaching a human.
title: Risk budget and autonomy envelope

name: coding_agent
concept: A real tool-calling model in a LangGraph ToolNode loop lists, reads and patches files in a temporary repository and runs the tests; the graph ends when the tests pass, and reads outside the workspace are refused.
limitation: The repository is a one-function toy, and the test child process has an empty environment and timeout but is not a sandbox.
title: The smallest coding agent

name: iterative_repair
concept: A real model writes parse_price in a LangGraph propose -> test loop against hidden tests; failing test names are fed back as the next message and cases that passed before and now fail are flagged as regressions.
limitation: In the runs observed the model passed within two attempts, so no regression appeared; the regression flag is not exercised in every run; the test child process is not a sandbox.
title: Iterative repair

name: computer_use
concept: A real model grounds 'submit the form' in a toy screen observation; a LangGraph interrupt() pauses for approval while the layout shifts, and clicking stale coordinates presses Delete while re-grounding presses Submit and verifies the postcondition.
limitation: The screen is an in-memory list of labelled buttons with coordinates; no screenshot, browser or desktop is used.
title: Computer use

name: multimodal
concept: A real vision model reads a clear and a smudged package label rendered as PNG and passed in a LangChain image message; structured evidence with confidence is compared against the order record, escalating the mismatch and asking for re-capture when unreadable.
limitation: One recorded run with a Pillow-rendered label; confidence values are the model's self-reports, not calibrated.
title: Multimodal reasoning

name: self_improvement
concept: A real model classifies support requests through a LangChain prompt chain, another call revises the prompt from development failures, and candidates are chosen on validation data and promoted only on held-out gain without a per-label regression.
limitation: The splits are tiny (4/4/8 rows), so scores are noisy; no weights are trained, only the prompt text changes.
title: Prompt self-improvement

name: experience_learning
concept: Episodes in a LangGraph store are promoted to scoped lessons with evidence and provenance only above success thresholds, and a real tool-calling agent chooses actions for new tasks with naive or validated lessons in its context.
limitation: Episodes are fixtures, thresholds are illustrative, the chosen actions are not executed, and the agent's choice for unpromoted cases varies between runs.
title: Experience learning

name: reward_optimization
concept: A real tool-calling model is told a 'closed ticket' proxy reward and its action sequence joins a LangChain RunnableParallel policy search; the proxy selects closing without fixing, while the true objective or a hard rule selects solving.
limitation: A three-policy search over deterministic episodes, not reinforcement learning; the prompted model did not game the proxy in the runs observed.
title: Reward hacking
